_note: Field elites -- BD2-style stationary rares. struktured 2026-09-06: 'it's not moving around, it just sits there on the overworld menacingly glowing or radiating. You have to make contact to decide to fight it and it's unfairly strong -- pinned to be stronger than your party by a lot. Rare drops/exp if you beat it though.'
_scaling_is_data_on_purpose: He asked for the scaling to be data, not code. EncounterSystem._create_enemy_data reads this table when a monster carries field_elite -- so retuning difficulty is a JSON edit, and the same numbers are visible to tests without executing a battle.
_pinned_above_the_party: level_offset and the multipliers are applied against the PARTY AVERAGE at the moment the fight starts, never against the monster's authored level. That is the whole point: a field elite is unfair at every point in the game, not just at the level it was written for.
_spawn_note: chance_per_fill is rolled once per spawner fill tick (CHECK_INTERVAL 3.0s) and only when no elite is alive. MEASURED 2026-09-09, correcting the claim this note used to make: 0.012 over a 3s tick is a mean of ~4.2 minutes to the roll landing, so a 20-minute session sees roughly 4 sightings, not the 'one' this line previously asserted. Left as measured rather than retuned to the old target -- struktured asked for these MORE often ('I never see one'), so 4 is likely closer to the ask than 1, and retuning a feel parameter he has not playtested would be inventing an answer. min_seconds_between is the floor after one is fought. An elite is exempt from distance culling, so an unfought one stays where it is and holds the single max_alive slot until you deal with it.
_dev_how_to_force_a_spawn: TO SEE ONE IMMEDIATELY (first playtest, or any time you want to check the look): set chance_per_fill to 1.0 and min_seconds_between to 0. One then appears at the next spawner tick (~3s) every time you walk into fresh ground, and every time you leave and return. Put the numbers back afterwards -- at 1.0 they are no longer rare, which is the entire point of them. Nothing else needs changing and no rebuild is required: this file is read at spawn time.
_roster_note: One per world. Medieval gets a purpose-built Dark Knight (struktured named it). The others promote that world's apex species -- already flavored as the top of its food chain -- rather than inventing five more monsters nobody asked for. Suburban's is the neighborhood dog ON PURPOSE: a perfectly ordinary dog, radiating, unfairly strong, is this game's humor rather than a failure of nerve.
